title: Warmly Spiced Moroccan Lamb Mechoui
description: A traditional Moroccan dish featuring lamb slow-cooked in a blend of aromatic spices, with a twist of balsamic vinegar and a crispy exterior, served in a mechoui style, this recipe is low-calorie-friendly and does not include double-fry-kfc as it is not a part of traditional Moroccan cuisine.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a small bowl, mix together the cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Rub the spice mixture all over the lamb shoulder, making sure to coat it evenly.
Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat, then sear the lamb shoulder until browned on all sides.
Add the balsamic vinegar to the Dutch oven and bring to a boil, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Cover the Dutch oven with a lid and transfer it to the preheated oven.
Braise the lamb for 2 1/2 hours, or until it is tender and falls apart easily.
Remove the lamb from the oven and let it rest for 10 minutes before slicing it thinly against the grain.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot.
